title: Using Unity to develop AI-driven games makes me feel a bit stuck
author: ShoulderExtension420
selftext:
In the past year, I’ve used Unity + Cursor to create several games. The efficiency improvement has been significant, and it’s been really fun!

However, I feel that using a highly visual, interface-driven tool like Unity seems somewhat out of place in the AI era.

If the visual effects implementation were separated out into a tool like Rive, then the remaining logic implementation could be entirely done through vibe coding.

Perhaps in the future, open-source engines might integrate better with AI?

comments.author: whats_don_is_don
comments.body:
The video game industry really isn't as unique as people in the industry like to think (or people in any industry).

Whatever platform best supports AI tooling will win. A platform that is 20% more expensive to develop on because parts don't integrate with AI will last at legacy / slow moving companies, but it will become rarer.

This isn't some AI prediction, it's just the history of how tooling evolution changes any industry.

replies.author: buu_ai
replies.body: Totally agree! Artists that refuse to use AI tools will be left behind as well

replies.author: whats_don_is_don
replies.body:
This is a more interesting prediction - there are still artists who refuse to use computers. 

But generally, for **any job**, if you position yourself as just doing some tasks along the funnel to delivering the end value (ie an enjoyable game), you're at risk to get automated away.

Technology puts a constant pressure on automating away parts of the funnel to deliver final value. 

I see a lot of people / artists not think this way, and then feel pressure when they see their industry changing. Instead of thinking that 'my job is being automated away', you should think 'I have X years seeing how the sausage is made, and know the most valuable spots to be in that funnel". As you go from having \~5 years in an industry to \~20 years in it, this is the vision you need to gain if you want increased stability / seniority.
